title: The Great Depression in the USA
body: Before the 1930s, most economists followed the classical tradition: they believed that all labourers who were ready to work would find employment and all factories would work at full capacity. The Great Depression of 1929 and the years after it shook this belief. In the countries of Europe and North America, output and employment fell by huge amounts. Demand for goods in the market was low, many factories were lying idle and workers were thrown out of jobs. In the USA, between 1929 and 1933, the unemployment rate rose from 3 per cent to 25 per cent, while aggregate output fell by about 33 per cent. The unemployment rate is the number of people who are not working and are looking for jobs, divided by the total number of people who are working or looking for jobs. These events forced economists to explain how an economy could suffer long-lasting unemployment.
